name: Beclometasone dipropionate
route_note: Inhaled (including extra-fine HFA aerosols) for asthma/COPD; nasal spray; topical; gastro-resistant oral tablets in some countries for ulcerative colitis
originator: Schering Corporation; inhaled use developed by Glaxo

discovery.note: Chlorinated prednisolone-type diester patented as a topical steroid; Glaxo showed its value by inhalation.

rx_status: prescription; nasal spray OTC in some countries
tagline: The first widely used inhaled corticosteroid for asthma
summary: Beclometasone dipropionate is a prodrug glucocorticoid whose introduction as an aerosol in 1972 established inhaled corticosteroids as the basis of asthma treatment. It is used by inhalation, nasally and on the skin, and in fixed combinations with formoterol.
mechanism: Esterases in the lung and other tissues convert beclometasone dipropionate to beclometasone 17-monopropionate, which has much higher affinity for the glucocorticoid receptor.
The activated receptor represses inflammatory gene transcription and induces anti-inflammatory mediators, reducing airway inflammation and hyperresponsiveness.
uses: COPD (with formoterol, with or without glycopyrronium)
Mild to moderate ulcerative colitis (oral, some countries)

history.title: Patented
history.detail: Beclometasone dipropionate is patented by Schering.

history.title: Inhaled asthma therapy
history.detail: Glaxo launches Becotide in the UK, the first widely used inhaled corticosteroid.

history.title: US approval
history.detail: Inhaled beclomethasone (Vanceril, Schering) is approved in the US.

history.title: Extra-fine HFA aerosol
history.detail: Qvar, an HFA solution aerosol with smaller particles, is approved in the US.

pk.bioavailability: Inhaled active metabolite largely lung-absorbed; oral contribution small

facts: The 1972 launch of Becotide is generally regarded as the start of inhaled corticosteroid therapy for asthma.
Extra-fine beclometasone aerosols are dosed lower than older CFC formulations because more drug reaches the small airways.
